"Purified great wisdom has already departed from all poisons; the fiery pits have all been extinguished, and the household is as pure as it was originally, no different from before—all this is due to the majestic spiritual power of the Dharma King."
At that time, the elder Guhagupta conceived great faith toward the Buddha and covered the Buddha’s body with exquisite robes worth hundreds of thousands of millions of billions.
Having covered [his head], he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

I was originally foolish and followed the teachings of the six masters. Now, before the Buddha, I repent with a sincere heart. Because my father in a former life revered and believed in the non-Buddhist paths, I followed my father’s lead and committed such offenses."

"Now, because of Candraprabha, I have been led to believe in the Buddha. I now repent with earnestness and a sincere heart; I shall commit no further transgressions. I pray that the Buddha will save me.
At that time.

The devas of the form realm again raised a great sound and scattered celestial *utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, *puṇḍarīka*, *māndārava*, and *mahāmāndārava* flowers, which filled the ground until they reached the knees in height.
The elder addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

My son Candraprabha is difficult to encounter even in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas. Out of compassion for me, he has been born into my family; he has skillfully expounded for me the merits of all Buddhas, and his kindness over hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas is difficult to repay. He then scattered priceless pearl necklaces upon the Buddha.

At that time, because the World-Honored One wished to inspire deep faith in the elder Guhagupta, he employed his supernormal powers to manifest clouds of hundreds of thousands of millions of colors made of various jewels.

At that time, Lu-hi-da-shu (translated as "Red Horse"), a name for a deity, and Pi-zhi-lo-sha, also a name for a deity, scattered various multicolored jewel flowers, radiant with light, upon the Buddha. An incalculable number (*asaṃkhyeya*) of bodhisattvas manifested immeasurable supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*) and arrived before the Buddha, desiring to transform and guide hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of sentient beings.

At that time, the elder Guṇaprabha, the youth Candraprabha, the youth Guṇākara, and the others felt great joy in their hearts; they prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, repented with a sincere mind, and spoke these words:
“Alas, how marvelous!

The supernatural transformations of Śākyamuni Tathāgata are inconceivable; he is difficult to encounter even in hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas, let alone give rise to pure faith. A Buddha’s appearance in the world is difficult to meet even in immeasurable billions of kalpas.

This youth Candraprabha possesses great wisdom; he has seen immeasurable billions of Buddhas throughout the ten directions, traveling through all Buddha-worlds to bow his head, take refuge, and prostrate before the Buddhas. Just as Śākyamuni Tathāgata sees the Buddhas of the ten directions, so too does the youth Candraprabha; he is able to see the Buddhas of the ten directions and pay them homage by touching their feet, and he never forgets the Dharma he hears from those Buddhas.

At that time, the Tathāgata saw that the male and female members of the Elder Guhagupta’s household—both great and small—as well as the youth Candraprabha, had already conceived right faith in the Triple Gem; they prostrated, offered praise, extensively planted roots of goodness, and increased their mental cultivation. Thereupon, the Tathāgata smiled, as is the manner of all Buddhas, and from his face issued immeasurable tens of millions of flames of light of various colors. From each of his forty teeth and four canine fangs, he emitted immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of rays of light in blue, yellow, red, white, purple, and crystal colors. These lights shone universally upon all Buddha-fields in the eastern direction; likewise, they shone everywhere throughout the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir. Once the illumination was complete, the light circled the body three times and re-entered through the crown of his head.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Guṇaparyutthānavinivṛtta rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"For what cause and condition does the Tathāgata manifest this smile?
The Buddhas do not smile without a cause.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Vigatālambanaguṇa, saying:
“Excellent! Excellent,
son of good family!”

That you are able to ask the Buddha about such causes and conditions shows that you have already, throughout immeasurable thousands of myriads of koṭis of kalpas in the past, constantly inquired into this meaning; it is now, by virtue of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, that you are able to ask about this meaning.
"Good son!
Listen now with a sincere mind and attend closely;
I shall speak for you. Good son!"
"Do you now see this elder Guhagupta’s eldest son, the youth Candraprabha?
"Indeed, I have seen him," he replied.
The Buddha said:

"This youth is able to inspire pure faith in sentient beings who have not yet developed it, to discipline those who are not yet disciplined, and to bring to maturity those who are not yet matured; he acts as a spiritual friend to his father."

Why is this? Because he was able to teach and transform his father through the Dharma of a Guide, establishing immeasurable thousands of millions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeya sentient beings within the Buddha-dharma, causing them to give rise to faith and ensuring they would certainly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Furthermore, after my parinirvāṇa, this youth will protect and uphold my Dharma in future ages; he will make offerings to the Tathāgata, receive and maintain the Buddha-Dharma, establish the Buddha-Dharma, and praise the Buddha-Dharma.

In a future age, during the final period of the Buddha-dharma, within the land of Jambudvīpa in the great state of Sui, he will become a great king named Mahācaryā (Great Practice), who will cause all sentient beings within the realm of Sui to have faith in the Buddha-dharma and plant various roots of goodness.

“At that time, King Mahācārin shall offer my bowl with great faith and the power of great majesty. After several years, my bowl shall reach the kingdom of Śākala; from there it will proceed in succession to the Great Sui Kingdom. That King Mahācārin shall make grand offerings at the site of the Buddha’s bowl, and he shall further be able to uphold all the Buddha’s teachings and extensively transcribe hundreds of thousands of billions of Mahāyāna Vaipulya sūtras. He shall establish the Dharma-treasuries of the Buddhas in various places, calling them ‘Dharma-stūpas,’ and he shall fashion hundreds of thousands of Buddha images and hundreds of thousands of Buddha stūpas, causing immeasurable sentient beings to attain non-retrogression within the Buddha’s Dharma and to attain irreversible faith.”

“By virtue of these causes and conditions of making offerings, that king shall always be born together with immeasurable, incalculable, boundless, and ineffable Buddhas; he shall always serve as a wheel-turning sage-king in all Buddha-fields and shall constantly encounter all Buddhas.”

He made offerings, paid homage, showed respect, and offered praise to the entire Sangha of the Buddha’s Dharma; he constructed stupas and monasteries, and dedicated all manner of articles of pleasure as gifts.

Having spent half his life in this way, he renounced the five desires, left the household life for homelessness, and purely cultivated the holy life as a practice of Dharma-offering. When all the men and women within Jambudvīpa saw that the king had gone forth, they also followed him in leaving the household life to purely cultivate the holy life.

"This King Mahācaryā has accomplished the supreme vows of immeasurable bodhisattvas and attained great supernormal powers. Having practiced the bodhisattva path for incalculable eons, the number of sentient beings he has transformed in each individual eon is beyond all calculation, ineffable, and immeasurable; they have all been established securely within the Buddha-dharma."

Just as he transforms sentient beings during one eon, so it is throughout all eons. This bodhisattva thus abides, and after immeasurable, boundless, and ineffable sentient beings have been established in the Buddha-dharma, they shall, in their final body, attain Buddhahood. They will appear in the world as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān named Vimalacandranirāraṃbaṇāsaṅgamahāvyūha. The world where he appears shall be named Unobstructed (Anāvaraṇa).

That Buddha’s body is vast and expansive; he possesses immeasurable radiance, immeasurable flames of light, immeasurable supernormal powers, immeasurable preaching of the Dharma, immeasurable assemblies of followers, immeasurable turnings of the wheel of Dharma, and immeasurable physical marks, teaching and transforming immeasurable sentient beings.

"When that Buddha was about to enter parinirvāṇa, he bestowed a prophecy upon the elder Guptadatta, saying: 'He shall become a buddha, named Asamasamagātra Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.'"

Those members of the householder Guṇapāla’s family who, upon seeing my miraculous transformations, gave rise to the bodhicitta, shall all become buddhas in that kalpa, each with their own respective names and in successive order.

Devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others who, upon seeing me manifest supernatural transformations in the home of the elder Guhagupta, gave rise to the bodhicitta—none of them shall ever regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
in various lands throughout the worlds of the ten directions, each with their own distinct names, they shall all attain buddhahood.
"In this way, noble son!
This youth Candraprabha has, throughout immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas in the past, taught and transformed the elder Guṇapāla."
"This youth and the elder Śrīgupta shall, in future ages, always be born in worlds where Buddhas reside, and they shall teach and transform immeasurable sentient beings.

When these causes and conditions for the bestowal of the prediction of enlightenment upon the youth Candraprabha and the elder Śrīgupta were being spoken, immeasurable worlds shook in six ways; a great light shone everywhere, and there fell rains of various celestial flowers, various celestial jewels, celestial necklaces, celestial canopies, various celestial robes, celestial sandalwood powder, celestial aloeswood incense, celestial tagara incense, celestial utpala lotuses, and celestial padma lotuses.

The celestial musicians produced subtle and wondrous sounds, as did the songs and chants of the devas; all of these were due to the supernatural power of the Buddha and the power of the roots of goodness cultivated by Candraprabha in his past lives. This was for the sake of transforming the householder Śrīgupta and his retinue, and also to transform the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others.

At that time, the son of the great elder Guṇapāla, named Guṇa, beheld the various supernormal powers of the Buddha and saw the gods, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings presenting great offerings. He addressed the Buddha with a verse in praise, saying:
"Homage to the Buddha of Great Wisdom, The Tathāgata, Lion of the Śākyas!
If one can give rise to faith, One shall obtain great benefit."
Previously you had faith in non-Buddhist paths, And thereby committed various evil deeds;
Now, by placing faith in the World-Honored One, You have attained such great benefit.
Seeing this inconceivable marvel, who would not believe in the Buddha?
Even such persons of grave offenses, through the power of the Buddha, give rise to faith.
With single-minded reverence and faith in the Supreme Guide who has transcended the world,
they shall not fall into the various evil realms for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of kalpas.
The elder committed great transgressions, yet now he has attained pure faith;
by virtue of these causes and conditions of faith, the Tathāgata grants him a prophecy.
The elder recognizes his own sins, and in his heart arises great sorrow and distress.
Now that you have attained faith, you shall obtain immeasurable merit.
Having removed evil views from your mind, you confess all transgressions;
before the Buddha, the World-Honored One, you cultivate a pure heart.
Because you have single-mindedly placed faith in the Buddha, by virtue of these causal conditions of faith,
you shall become a Buddha in a future life— an inconceivable Dharma King.
Having initially conceived malice toward the Buddha, you now give rise to deep faith.
By virtue of the causes and conditions of giving, one attains a treasury of pure karma.
Those who conceive faith in the Buddha—everyone places their trust in such a person;
the mass of that person’s merit and virtue is beyond all measure.

At that time, the elder Śrīgupta prostrated with his head at the feet of the Buddha and all the arhats, as well as the entire assembly of bodhisattvas; having done so, he served them food and drink of a hundred flavors in succession.

When the World-Honored One had finished preaching this Dharma, the Bodhisattva Vigatāśrayaguṇa, the youth Candraprabha, and the elder Guhagupta, together with all their internal and external retinues, the assembly of great bodhisattvas, and the entire multitude including devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and others, were all greatly rejoiced; they paid homage and respectfully practiced it.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Elder Guṇapāla, Scroll II.
